property_summary: sendTo can only succeed when caller is the contract owner (i.e., non-owner callers must not be able to transfer funds).
Only the contract owner can successfully call sendTo (i.e., calls from non-owners revert).
If the caller is not the transaction origin (tx.origin), then sendTo must revert (only the deployer/owner may succeed), so non-owner callers cannot successfully invoke sendTo.
If this test contract is acting as an intermediary (address(this) != tx.origin), then calling c.sendTo(...) must revert.
When this contract is used as an intermediary (address(this) != tx.origin), calling c.sendTo(receiver, amount) must revert.

For every call to sendTo(receiver, amount), the reference contract only allows the owner (deployer) to successfully invoke it; the mutant instead allows only non-owners which causes calls from the owner to be rejected (or vice versa), so there exist inputs (owner as caller) that make the mutant behavior differ.

For every admissible caller and arguments, only the contract deployer (owner) can successfully call sendTo; the mutant inverted that check and rejects the owner, so there exist inputs (caller == owner) where the mutant fails but the reference succeeds.

For every caller address and nonzero amount with nonzero receiver, the reference contract allows the deployer (owner) to successfully call sendTo, so whenever the caller equals the deployer and receiver != address(0) and amount > 0 the call succeeds; the mutant inverts the owner check and thus rejects calls from the deployer, breaking this rule for those inputs.

For any caller and nonzero receiver/amount, if the caller is the contract deployer (owner) then sendTo succeeds (does not revert) on the reference C; the mutant inverts the owner check and will revert when the owner calls, so this rule is violated for inputs where the fuzzed caller equals the deployer and receiver != address(0) and amount > 0.

For any caller A, receiver R (nonzero) and amount > 0, if A is the owner then calling sendTo(R,amount) transfers the amount out of the contract (call succeeds and reduces address(c).balance by amount); the mutant inverts the owner check and thus for owner callers the mutant call will revert (or not send) breaking this transfer property for some inputs.
After construction by owner, calling sendTo with amount > 0 never decreases c's balance when receiver is the zero address (P prevents sending to zero, M allows it).
